raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Extend the preload framework from weights-only to host-side artifacts and make the FlashInfer autotune table the first one.

The daemon gains a bounded, exactly-keyed artifact store served over its existing Unix socket, so any local process can fetch the table, not only the engine that owns the GPU. An engine that finds a table loads it and skips the autotune pass outright; an engine that has to tune hands its table back, so the pass runs once per GPU rather than once per restart. A hit still raises the Kimi K3 KDA projection-overlap limit that the pass sets on the model, since the table does not carry it.

`vllm preload --preload-autotune` runs one throwaway engine against the ready daemons so the pass and the JIT compilation happen at preload time, leaving the table on the daemons for every engine that follows. That engine resolves its defaults under the same usage context as `vllm serve`, since they feed the config hash the table is keyed by, and drops preload's disk-loader config, which its IPC loader would reject.

Hmmm, will it be too heavy to fully start a whole engine for preload?
Not a blocker, but I'm thinking whether to reorganize the preload components to something like `vllm/preload`? 🤔

I think we can dump autotuned configs to disk cache through FI API, do we still need to hold it on daemon and transport through socket?
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c83935b3008553c72b1bad09f842b4c99b7fa47f/vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_autotune_cache.py#L24-L41
This is mainly for d2d seeding: the tuned table rides along with the weights to a new replica, often on another host, where the local disk cache isn't visible. The disk cache is unchanged.
I think mamba block size can be safely removed, but I'm not sure about `block_size`

 The daemon itself must load from disk; passing `--load-format ipc_cache` to
 `vllm preload` is an error.
 
+## Preloading the FlashInfer autotune cache
+
+FlashInfer has several implementations of each operation and chooses between
+them by benchmarking. vLLM runs that pass during kernel warmup and persists the
+result per rank in the on-disk FlashInfer autotune cache (under
+`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`, or `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR`), so a later engine
+with the same configuration loads the tuned configs instead of profiling again.
+Normally the first serving engine pays for the pass, and on a large MoE model it
+dominates what is left of the startup time once the weights come from the
+daemon.
+
+Unless FlashInfer autotune is disabled (`--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`),
+`vllm preload` pays it at preload time: each daemon runs the autotune pass in
+place — profiling dummy runs against the shard it already holds — after
+loading and before binding its socket, then writes the cache:
+
+```bash
+vllm preload --model /path/to/model --tensor-parallel-size 4
+```
+
 ## How it works

inline_comments.body: Hmmm, will it be too heavy to fully start a whole engine for preload?
Not a blocker, but I'm thinking whether to reorganize the preload components to something like `vllm/preload`? 🤔

I think we can dump autotuned configs to disk cache through FI API, do we still need to hold it on daemon and transport through socket?
https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/c83935b3008553c72b1bad09f842b4c99b7fa47f/vllm/model_executor/warmup/flashinfer_autotune_cache.py#L24-L41
This is mainly for d2d seeding: the tuned table rides along with the weights to a new replica, often on another host, where the local disk cache isn't visible. The disk cache is unchanged.
I think mamba block size can be safely removed, but I'm not sure about `block_size`
